name: code-block
purpose: Use CodeBlock to show code, config or JSON the person reads or copies, including read-only diffs (a tab's `original`); for code the person edits use CodeEditor, and for build, deploy or runtime log lines use LogViewer. Read-only code viewer for docs, API examples, and configuration previews. Supports four Figma-documented layouts that share one monolithic shell: 1. **Language switcher** ([4567:33761](https://www.figma.com/design/t97pXRs7xME3SJDs5iZ5RF/Webkit?node-id=4567-33761)) — tabbed snippets with a sliding pill, optional filename bar, syntax highlighting, and copy. 2. **Show filename** ([4567:30198](https://www.figma.com/design/t97pXRs7xME3SJDs5iZ5RF/Webkit?node-id=4567-30198)) — single snippet with a raised filename bar (language icon + name), no tabs. 3. **Diff** ([4567:29012](https://www.figma.com/design/t97pXRs7xME3SJDs5iZ5RF/Webkit?node-id=4567-29012)) — per-line added/removed markers (`+`/`-`), semantic row backgrounds, and a 2 px leading bar; no tabs or filename bar. 4. **Highlighted line** ([4567:31473](https://www.figma.com/design/t97pXRs7xME3SJDs5iZ5RF/Webkit?node-id=4567-31473)) — one active line with info background and leading bar; no tabs or filename bar. Two more regions serve docs: a **label header** — a 40 px bar naming the block (`</>` + "Shell", "JavaScript", from the active tab's label or the language's readable name, or `title`) when `showLabel` is on and there is no tab strip or filename bar — and the **output** type (`type="output"`): what a command prints, drawn flat in `--text-muted` on `--bg-canvas` under an "Output" label, with no copy control by default. A command block and its output are always two blocks. The **label header holds the copy control** at its end, and so does the tab strip, or the filename bar when there is one, so the control never covers the first lines of code on a phone (`data-copy-gutter` marks the root only while the block has no header at all and the copy sits in a column of its own at the end of the code instead, so no line runs under it) and is `sticky` at the top of the nearest scroller, so a long block keeps its language and copy in view. Its divider shows only when `bordered`; unbordered, header and code share one fill (the `StreamingResponse` look). The other regions render conditionally from tab data. Tab header appears when `tabs.length > 1`. Filename bar appears when the active tab sets `fileName`. Diff and highlight decorations come from `lineChanges` and `highlightedLine` on the active tab. **Syntax highlighting** is driven by the active tab's `language` and resolves to one of these tokenisers, all of which emit the same seven token types (`keyword`, `string`, `function`, `type`, `punctuation`, `identifier`, `comment`) so every language shares the one `--code-syntax-*` palette:
useWhen: Read-only code in docs, API examples or configuration previews that readers copy from.
The same snippet in several languages, switched by tabs (one `tabs` entry per language).
Showing a change as a diff (`lineChanges`) or pointing at one line (`highlightedLine`) on the active tab.

Showing what changed between two versions of a file — a configuration before and after a deploy, the code a release replaces — by passing the previous version as the tab's `original`: the block computes the line diff itself and draws it unified or side by side (`diffView`).
avoidWhen: The content is build or deploy output with timestamps and log levels → use `log-viewer`.
It is a marketing band that pairs a claim with its code → use `feature-scroll-section` with code items.
It is a terminal session of CLI commands on a product page → use `cli-terminal-section`.
You only need to copy one short value (a token, an ID) without showing a block → use `copy-button`.
The reader edits the new version beside the old one → use `code-editor` in diff mode. A read-only diff is always this block with `original`, never a read-only code editor.
related: `copy-button` — the copy control CodeBlock embeds; use it alone for one-line values.
`code-editor` — the editable surface; its diff mode is for editing beside an original, while a read-only diff is this block.
`log-viewer` — terminal-style viewer for CI and deploy logs.
`feature-scroll-section` — page section whose steps can each pin a code sample (`code`).
`scroll-area` — the scroll container the code region runs in.
bestPractices: Put the source on each tab's `code`. There is no top-level `code` prop, and a tab without a `value` or a `code` is dropped.
Set `language` on every tab. Only JavaScript/TypeScript, shell, HCL, GraphQL and Markdown are tokenised; anything else renders as flat text.
Use `default-value` for the initial tab, and `v-model` only when something outside the block must follow the selected tab.

Prefer `original` to a hand-written `lineChanges` list whenever both versions are at hand: the diff stays right when either version changes. Keep `unified` in narrow columns and use `split` where the block has room for two columns of code.
Set `:copyable="false"` on decorative blocks, and `:bordered="false"` when the block sits inside a surface that already frames it.
Keep `animate-lines` for marketing layouts; leave it off in docs and console screens.
Do: keep a command block to what the reader runs — the copy control copies exactly that. Put what it prints in a second block with `type="output"` (or in prose).

Don't: write expected output into the command, as a `# HTTP/2 200` comment or as unprompted lines after a `$ ` prompt — the reader pastes it into the terminal. The `webkit/no-output-in-command` lint warns on it.
Do: turn `show-label` on in docs (`DocCodeGroup` does by default) so every block is titled with its language; set `title` only when the language name is not the right title.

props.name: tabs
props.doc: Tab definitions with label, value, code, and optional language, filename, diff, or highlight metadata.

props.name: code
props.doc: Code of a single snippet, used when `tabs` is empty.

props.name: language
props.doc: Language of the single `code` snippet (highlighting and the label header).

props.name: showLineNumbers
props.doc: Shows a fixed-width gutter with zero-padded line numbers before each code line (the same name as `code-editor`).

props.name: copyAriaLabel
props.doc: Accessible name for the copy control (forwarded to CopyButton's aria-label). Empty uses the locale catalog (`Copy code`).

props.name: copyable
props.doc: Shows the copy control. Unset, a `code` block shows it and an `output` block does not; turn it off for a decorative block nobody copies from.

props.name: type
props.doc: What the block holds: `code` the reader runs or reads, or `output` — what a command prints — drawn flat and muted under an "Output" label, without a copy control.

props.name: showLabel
props.doc: Shows a header naming the block when there is no tab strip or file name: the active tab's label, else the language's readable name (Shell, JavaScript). Docs blocks show it.

props.name: title
props.doc: Text of the label header; empty uses the tab label or the language name, or "Output" for an `output` block.

props.name: animateLines
props.doc: Staggered line entrance for website layouts: each line slides from `-8px` with opacity `0 → 1`, `40ms` apart.

props.name: bordered
props.doc: Draw the outer card border around the block. On by default; set `:bordered="false"` to render the block flush when it sits inside a surface that already frames it. Internal dividers (tab header, filename bar) are unaffected; the label header's divider goes with the border.

props.name: diffView
props.doc: How a tab with an `original` draws the diff the block computes: `unified` (one column) or `split` (side by side).

events.name: copy
events.notes: Fires after the active tab code is copied to the clipboard.

slots.name: tab-icon
slots.notes: Leading mark before a tab's label in the tab strip; nothing renders when it is not filled.
